chunks: 53 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I asked him about a man who missed the fasting of the three days during Hajj. He said: 'Whoever misses the fasting of three days during Hajj, provided it was not deliberate abandonment, then he must fast in Mecca as long as he does not leave it. If his mount refuses to stay with him, let him fast on the road.'

key_terms.صَوْمُ الثَّلَاثَةِ أَيَّامِ: the fasting of the three days

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the three days of fasting during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical application of *Qada* (making up) missed fasts for pilgrims, emphasizing that the obligation is tied to the state of being in Mecca rather than the ritual of Hajj itself. The specific detail regarding the mount (*jammal*) refusing to stay highlights the classical juristic consideration of physical constraints and ease (*rukhas*) in applying legal rulings during travel. It reflects the Shia scholarly focus on distinguishing between deliberate neglect and unavoidable omission when determining the location and manner of compensation.
